Singles and doubles

A single is one target from one trap. In both disciplines two shots may be fired at it, so if you miss you may fire again with the second barrel. A pair, or double, is two targets that go together: one call, and you shoot both.

Report pair (double on report): the call releases the first target, and the shot at it releases the second. In Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ the second comes 0 to 3 seconds after that shot. The order is fixed. “Report” means the sound of the shot, not a written report.

Simultaneous pair (“simo”; British coaches also say “true pair”): both targets leave at the same moment and may be shot in any order. They come from one or two traps; in Compak® Sporting always from two different traps.

Following pair, which FITASC calls rafale: two targets from the same trap on the same flight path, the second leaving as soon as the trap has reloaded. You may shoot either one first. It exists only in Sporting™: a Compak® Sporting double is on report or simultaneous.

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

Two cartridges for the double, and both may be fired at one target. If one shot breaks both targets, both count as hits (the referee calls “one” for each).

Compak® Sporting

One cartridge per target. Deliberately firing both shots at one target is scored zero-zero (both targets counted as missed). If one shot breaks both targets, they do not count as two hits. On a double on report, the first target's result stands and the double is thrown again for the second. On a simultaneous double, it is a No Bird and the double is repeated; the third time it happens, it is scored zero-zero.

Tip: How doubles are scored, including zero-zero and a No Bird in a pair, is explained in Doubles: how they are shot and scored.

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

On a Sporting™ stand the squad shoots the singles first, then the doubles. Before shooting, simultaneous and rafale doubles are thrown so the shooters can see them (they are shown to the first shooter of the squad); report pairs are not shown.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 16 · Which doubles are shown

A Sporting™ layout gives 25 targets: 15 singles and 5 doubles, and the doubles use only targets already shown as singles from the same stand. A Compak® Sporting round is also 25 targets, five per station, in one of three mixes: five singles; three singles and one double; or one single and two doubles.

Tip: Before you call for a double, many coaches suggest planning both targets: which one first, where you break each, and where your eyes go for the second. More in Pairs: the second target.

Key points

  • Single: one target, two shots allowed.
  • Report pair: the shot at the first releases the second; order fixed.
  • Rafale (following pair): same trap, same line, Sporting™ only.
  • Simultaneous (true pair): both at once, any order.
  • Sporting™: both cartridges may go at one target; Compak® Sporting: one per target.

Did you know?

Rafale is French for a “burst” or “gust”: the targets leave one after the other as fast as the trap can reload.

Stand Talk

  • Coach It's on report — finish the first one properly, the second waits for your shot.

    Meaning: The second target only comes when the shooter fires at the first, so there is no need to rush the first.

  • Coach Simo: take the rabbit first, the teal will wait for you.

    Meaning: In the simultaneous pair shoot the rabbit first, because the teal stays in the air longer.

  • Coach Rafale — after the first, come straight back to the trap for the second.

    Meaning: Both targets come from the same trap; after the first shot, return eyes and gun towards the trap to pick up the second.

  • Coach True pair from the tower, five of them.

    Meaning: Five simultaneous pairs thrown from the tower (British coaches’ wording).

Check yourself · 3 questions

  1. In a report pair, what releases the second target?

    1. A second call
    2. The referee's signal
    3. The shot at the first target
    4. A timer of exactly 5 seconds
    Answer

    The shot at the first target

    “On report” means on the sound of the shot: firing at the first target releases the second.

  2. In Compak® Sporting a shooter deliberately fires both cartridges at the first target of a simultaneous double. Result?

    1. Allowed, as in Sporting™
    2. Zero-zero
    3. No Bird and repeat
    4. Only the second target is zero
    Answer

    Zero-zero

    Compak® Sporting allows one cartridge per target of a double; deliberately firing both at one target is scored zero-zero. In Sporting™ it would be allowed.

  3. In which discipline are there rafale doubles?

    1. Only in Sporting™
    2. Only in Compak® Sporting
    3. In both
    Answer

    Only in Sporting™

    A rafale is two targets from one trap on one trajectory, a Sporting™ double. Compak® Sporting has only doubles on report and simultaneous doubles.
